chunks: And with this chain, it was said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Paradise: 'There is a door called the door of the Mujahideen.'
They proceed to it, and when it is opened, the Mujahideen are wearing their swords, the crowd is in the standing place, and the angels welcome them.
Whoever leaves Jihad, Allah will clothe him with humiliation and poverty in his livelihood, and destruction in his religion.
Surely Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, has made the greatness of my Ummah in the hooves of their horses and the points of their lances.

key_terms.الْجِهَاد: Striving or exertion in the path of God
key_terms.الْمَوْقِف: The standing place (of judgment or gathering)
key_terms.الْمُجَاهِدِينَ: Those who strive in the way of Allah
key_terms.مُتَقَلِّدُونَ: Wearing or carrying on the neck

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for Jihad in Paradise and the consequence of neglecting it?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* highlights the eschatological reward for Mujahideen, emphasizing that their entry into Paradise is marked by visible martial readiness and angelic welcome. It establishes a direct causal link between the neglect of Jihad and worldly/spiritual degradation (humiliation, poverty, and loss of faith), while affirming the Shia view that the honor of the Ummah is intrinsically tied to its military capability under the guidance of a just Imam.
